channel.title: Washington Jewish Week - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Washington Jewish Week (washingtonjewishweek.com)

item.title: Montgomery County Allocates $500K to Boost Security at Synagogues, Faith-Based Institutions
item.description: Montgomery County is providing an additional $500,000 to its Nonprofit Security Grant Program as concerns intensify due to violence in the Middle East and the recent attack on a Michigan synagogue.

item.title: Hadassah Leaders Lobby for US-Israel Relationship, Women’s Health
item.description: Though Hadassah’s Day of Impact had been planned months in advance, Iris Tishkoff felt that the current geopolitical landscape demanded action.

item.title: Jaclyn Talon Connects Young Jewish Families in Alexandria
item.description: Jaclyn Talon helps sustain Jewish life in her pocket of northern Virginia as a way to honor her maternal grandparents, who survived the Holocaust.

item.title: Bethesda's Rabbi Jonah Pesner Spearheads Social Justice Through Jewish Lens
item.description: Rabbi Jonah Pesner has a hefty job as the leader overseeing 850 Reform congregations across North America, keeping social justice and Jewish community top of mind.

item.title: Potomac Songwriter’s ‘My Name is Moses’ Makes Synagogue Debut
item.description: What if a central biblical figure was an ordinary person? That’s what a Potomac songwriter set out to explore through his song cycle, “My Name is Moses.”

item.title: German School Named for Albanian Who Saved Jews Sends Students to Tirana for Holocaust Remembrance
item.description: Sixteen-year-old Melisa Malo, a 10th-grader at the Gjimnazi Sami Frashëri here, first learned about the Holocaust four years ago when she attended an Albanian-language stage performance of “The Diary of Anne Frank.”

item.title: Helene Karpa
item.description: Helene Berman Karpa, 95, a third-generation native Washingtonian, died on March 20 at Suburban Hospital in Bethesda, Maryland.

item.title: Joseph Gottesman, Known for Quiet Devotion and Reliability, Dies at 87
item.description: Joseph Ernest Gottesman would linger after Shabbat services at Congregation Beth El in Bethesda, talking with people long after others had headed home.

item.title: Looking Back on 60 Years of Charles E. Smith Jewish Day School
item.description: Parents, faculty and alumni spoke to Charles E. Smith Jewish Day School’s tight-knit community, rigorous academics and teachers who go above and beyond for their students.

item.title: First Jewish Justice’s Great-Grandson Talks Interfaith Relations at Adat Shalom
item.description: Rev. Paul Brandeis Raushenbush, the great-grandson of the first Jewish Supreme Court justice, likes to say that he has an “interfaith heart.”
